sanskrit: vācā ca manasā caiva yathā nābhicarāmy aham tena satyena vibudhās tam eva pradiśantu me
english: By this truth — that neither in word nor in mind have I ever been unfaithful to him — let the wise gods point him out to me.

sanskrit: yathā devaiḥ sa me bhartā vihito niṣadhādhipaḥ tena satyena me devās tam eva pradiśantu me
english: By this truth — that the lord of Niṣadha was ordained to be my husband by the gods themselves — let the gods point him out to me.

sanskrit: svaṃ caiva rūpaṃ puṣyantu lokapālāḥ saheśvarāḥ yathāham abhijānīyāṃ puṇyaślokaṃ narādhipam
english: May the world-guardians together with Īśvara manifest their own true forms, so that I may recognize the glorious king Nala.

sanskrit: niśamya damayantyās tat karuṇaṃ paridevitam niścayaṃ paramaṃ tathyam anurāgaṃ ca naiṣadhe
english: Having heard Damayantī's piteous lamentation, her supreme and truthful resolve, and her passionate love for the Niṣadhan,

sanskrit: manoviśuddhiṃ buddhiṃ ca bhaktiṃ rāgaṃ ca bhārata yathoktaṃ cakrire devāḥ sāmarthyaṃ liṅgadhāraṇe
english: the gods, O Bhārata, perceiving the purity of her mind, her intelligence, her devotion, and her love, did just as she had asked — they assumed the power to display their own distinctive marks.

sanskrit: sāpaśyad vibudhān sarvān asvedān stabdhalocanān hṛṣitasragrajohīnān sthitān aspṛśataḥ kṣitim
english: She saw all the gods: unsweat­ing, with motionless eyes, their garlands fresh and untouched by dust, standing without touching the earth.

sanskrit: chāyādvitīyo mlānasrag rajaḥsvedasamanvitaḥ bhūmiṣṭho naiṣadhaś caiva nimeṣeṇa ca sūcitaḥ
english: But Nala the Niṣadhan was revealed by contrast: he had a shadow beside him, his garland was wilted, he was covered in dust and sweat, he stood on the ground, and he blinked his eyes.

sanskrit: sā samīkṣya tato devān puṇyaślokaṃ ca bhārata naiṣadhaṃ varayām āsa bhaimī dharmeṇa bhārata
english: Having thus distinguished the gods from the glorious Nala, O Bhārata, the daughter of Bhīma chose the Niṣadhan as her husband in accordance with dharma.

sanskrit: vilajjamānā vastrānte jagrāhāyatalocanā skandhadeśe 'sṛjac cāsya srajaṃ paramaśobhanām varayām āsa caivainaṃ patitve varavarṇinī
english: With downcast eyes, blushing, she took hold of the hem of her garment; on his shoulder she placed a supremely beautiful garland, and thus the fair-complexioned lady chose him as her lord.

sanskrit: tato hā heti sahasā śabdo mukto narādhipaiḥ devair maharṣibhiś caiva sādhu sādhv iti bhārata vismitair īritaḥ śabdaḥ praśaṃsadbhir nalaṃ nṛpam
english: Then suddenly a great cry of "Alas, alas!" burst forth from the assembled kings; and the gods and great sages, filled with wonder and praising King Nala, cried out "Excellent! Excellent!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vṛte tu naiṣadhe bhaimyā lokapālā mahaujasaḥ prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve nalāyāṣṭau varān daduḥ
english: Once Bhīma's daughter had chosen the Niṣadhan, the world-guardians of great majesty, their hearts filled with joy, all granted Nala eight boons.

sanskrit: pratyakṣadarśanaṃ yajñe gatiṃ cānuttamāṃ śubhām naiṣadhāya dadau śakraḥ prīyamāṇaḥ śacīpatiḥ
english: The lord of Śacī, Indra, delighted, granted to the Niṣadhan the gift of his direct visible presence at sacrifices and the most excellent and auspicious of goals in the afterlife.

sanskrit: agnir ātmabhavaṃ prādād yatra vāñchati naiṣadhaḥ lokān ātmaprabhāṃś caiva dadau tasmai hutāśanaḥ
english: Agni granted that he would arise wherever the Niṣadhan desired; and the fire-devourer gave him worlds radiant with Agni's own light.

sanskrit: yamas tv annarasaṃ prādād dharme ca paramāṃ sthitim apāṃpatir apāṃ bhāvaṃ yatra vāñchati naiṣadhaḥ
english: Yama granted him the finest flavor of food and supreme steadiness in dharma; and the lord of waters granted him the presence of water wherever the Niṣadhan might wish.

sanskrit: srajaṃ cottamagandhāḍhyāṃ sarve ca mithunaṃ daduḥ varān evaṃ pradāyāsya devās te tridivaṃ gatāḥ
english: All of them together gave him a garland richly laden with the finest fragrance, and also a pair of each gift. Having thus bestowed their boons upon him, those gods departed to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: pārthivāś cānubhūyāsyā vivāhaṃ vismayānvitāḥ damayantyāḥ pramuditāḥ pratijagmur yathāgatam
english: The assembled kings, having witnessed her wedding, departed each to his own home filled with wonder and delight at Damayantī's choice.

sanskrit: avāpya nārīratnaṃ tat puṇyaśloko 'pi pārthivaḥ reme saha tayā rājā śacyeva balavṛtrahā
english: Having won that jewel among women, the glorious king, that lord among men, rejoiced together with her, even as the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra delights with Śacī.

sanskrit: atīva mudito rājā bhrājamāno 'ṃśumān iva arañjayat prajā vīro dharmeṇa paripālayan
english: Exceedingly joyful, the king shone like the sun; that hero delighted his subjects, protecting them according to dharma.

sanskrit: īje cāpy aśvamedhena yayātir iva nāhuṣaḥ anyaiś ca kratubhir dhīmān bahubhiś cāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: The wise king also performed the horse-sacrifice, like Yayāti son of Nahuṣa, and many other rites with abundant sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: punaś ca ramaṇīyeṣu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca damayantyā saha nalo vijahārāmaropamaḥ
english: And again in charming forests and pleasure-groves, Nala, equal to the immortals, sported together with Damayantī.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa yajamānaś ca viharaṃś ca narādhipaḥ rarakṣa vasusaṃpūrṇāṃ vasudhāṃ vasudhādhipaḥ
english: Thus that lord of men, while performing sacrifices and taking his pleasures, protected the wealth-filled earth as lord of the earth.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca vṛte tu naiṣadhe bhaimyā lokapālā mahaujasaḥ yānto dadṛśur āyāntaṃ dvāparaṃ kalinā saha
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Now when the Niṣadhan had been chosen by Bhīma's daughter, the world-guardians of great majesty, as they were departing, saw Dvāpara and Kali approaching together.

sanskrit: athābravīt kaliṃ śakraḥ saṃprekṣya balavṛtrahā dvāpareṇa sahāyena kale brūhi kva yāsyasi
english: Then Indra, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, regarding Kali with Dvāpara as his companion, spoke: "Kali, tell me — where are you going?"

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt kaliḥ śakraṃ damayantyāḥ svayaṃvaram gatvāhaṃ varayiṣye tāṃ mano hi mama tadgatam
english: Then Kali answered Indra: "I am going to Damayantī's svayaṃvara to choose her for myself, for my mind is set upon her."

sanskrit: tam abravīt prahasyendro nirvṛttaḥ sa svayaṃvaraḥ vṛtas tayā nalo rājā patir asmatsamīpataḥ
english: Indra laughed and said to him: "That svayaṃvara is over. King Nala was chosen as her lord in our very presence."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu śakreṇa kaliḥ kopasamanvitaḥ devān āmantrya tān sarvān uvācedaṃ vacas tadā
english: Thus addressed by Indra, Kali was filled with rage; taking leave of all the gods, he then spoke these words:

sanskrit: devānāṃ mānuṣaṃ madhye yat sā patim avindata nanu tasyā bhaven nyāyyaṃ vipulaṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam
english: "She who found her husband among humans in the very midst of the gods — surely it is right that she should receive a great and fitting punishment."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu kalinā pratyūcus te divaukasaḥ asmābhiḥ samanujñāto damayantyā nalo vṛtaḥ
english: When Kali had spoken thus, the dwellers in heaven replied: "It was with our full consent that Nala was chosen by Damayantī."

sanskrit: kaś ca sarvaguṇopetaṃ nāśrayeta nalaṃ nṛpam yo veda dharmān akhilān yathāvac caritavrataḥ
english: "Who indeed would not seek shelter with King Nala, who is endowed with every virtue, who knows all the dharmas fully as they are, and who has always kept his vows?"

sanskrit: yasmin satyaṃ dhṛtir dānaṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ dhruvāṇi puruṣavyāghre lokapālasame nṛpe
english: "In that tiger among men, that king equal to the world-guardians, truth, steadfastness, generosity, austerity, purity, self-control, and tranquility are all firmly established."

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ sa śapen mūḍho hanyāc cātmānam ātmanā evaṃguṇaṃ nalaṃ yo vai kāmayec chapituṃ kale
english: "He would be a fool who desired to curse such a one as Nala, O Kali; he would curse himself and destroy himself by his own hand."

sanskrit: kṛcchre sa narake majjed agādhe vipule 'plave evam uktvā kaliṃ devā dvāparaṃ ca divaṃ yayuḥ
english: "He would sink into a dreadful, fathomless, and boundless hell from which there is no escape." Having spoken thus to Kali and Dvāpara, the gods departed to heaven.

sanskrit: tato gateṣu deveṣu kalir dvāparam abravīt saṃhartuṃ notsahe kopaṃ nale vatsyāmi dvāpara
english: Then, when the gods had gone, Kali said to Dvāpara: "I cannot contain my anger; I will dwell within Nala, O Dvāpara."

sanskrit: bhraṃśayiṣyāmi taṃ rājyān na bhaimyā saha raṃsyate tvam apy akṣān samāviśya kartuṃ sāhāyyam arhasi
english: "I will make him fall from his kingdom; he shall not enjoy happiness together with Bhīma's daughter. You too should enter into the dice and render your assistance."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evaṃ sa samayaṃ kṛtvā dvāpareṇa kaliḥ saha ājagāma tatas tatra yatra rājā sa naiṣadhaḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having thus made this pact together with Dvāpara, Kali came to that place where King Nala of Niṣadha dwelt.

sanskrit: sa nityam antaraprekṣī niṣadheṣv avasac ciram athāsya dvādaśe varṣe dadarśa kalir antaram
english: Watching constantly for an opportunity, he lived in Niṣadha for a long time; but only in the twelfth year did Kali find his opening.

sanskrit: kṛtvā mūtram upaspṛśya saṃdhyām āste sma naiṣadhaḥ akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucaṃ tatrainaṃ kalir āviśat
english: One day the Niṣadhan, having urinated and touched water, sat for the twilight prayers without having purified his feet; and at that moment Kali entered into him.

sanskrit: sa samāviśya tu nalaṃ samīpaṃ puṣkarasya ha gatvā puṣkaram āhedam ehi dīvya nalena vai
english: Having entered into Nala, he went straightway to Puṣkara and said to him: "Come, let us play at dice with Nala."

sanskrit: akṣadyūte nalaṃ jetā bhavān hi sahito mayā niṣadhān pratipadyasva jitvā rājan nalaṃ nṛpam
english: "With me by your side you will defeat Nala at the game of dice; win back Niṣadha, O king, by defeating King Nala."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kalinā puṣkaro nalam abhyayāt kaliś caiva vṛṣo bhūtvā gavāṃ puṣkaram abhyayāt
english: Thus instructed by Kali, Puṣkara approached Nala; and Kali himself, taking the form of a bull among cattle, accompanied Puṣkara.

sanskrit: āsādya tu nalaṃ vīraṃ puṣkaraḥ paravīrahā dīvyāvety abravīd bhrātā vṛṣeṇeti muhur muhuḥ
english: Having reached the heroic Nala, Puṣkara the destroyer of enemy heroes, his brother, said again and again: "Let us play at dice" — urged on by the bull.

sanskrit: na cakṣame tato rājā samāhvānaṃ mahāmanāḥ vaidarbhyāḥ prekṣamāṇāyāḥ paṇakālam amanyata
english: The great-souled king could not endure the challenge; with Vaidarbhī watching, he thought the time had come for staking his wager.

sanskrit: hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya yānayugyasya vāsasām āviṣṭaḥ kalinā dyūte jīyate sma nalas tadā
english: Possessed by Kali, Nala at that time was defeated at dice, losing silver, gold, vehicles, yoked animals, and garments.

sanskrit: tam akṣamadasaṃmattaṃ suhṛdāṃ na tu kaś cana nivāraṇe 'bhavac chakto dīvyamānam acetasam
english: Not one among his friends was able to restrain him as he played on, intoxicated with the madness of the dice, his mind utterly gone.

sanskrit: tataḥ paurajanaḥ sarvo mantribhiḥ saha bhārata rājānaṃ draṣṭum āgacchan nivārayitum āturam
english: Then all the townspeople together with the ministers, O Bhārata, came to see the king, to restrain the one overcome by affliction.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūta upāgamya damayantyai nyavedayat eṣa paurajanaḥ sarvo dvāri tiṣṭhati kāryavān
english: Then the charioteer came up and reported to Damayantī: "All the townspeople stand at the door with urgent business."

sanskrit: nivedyatāṃ naiṣadhāya sarvāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sthitāḥ amṛṣyamāṇā vyasanaṃ rājño dharmārthadarśinaḥ
english: "Let it be reported to the Niṣadhan that all his subjects stand here, unable to tolerate the calamity of the king who has always been a guardian of dharma and welfare."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā bāṣpakalayā vācā duḥkhena karśitā uvāca naiṣadhaṃ bhaimī śokopahatacetanā
english: Then she, Bhīma's daughter, wasted by sorrow, her mind struck by grief, spoke to the Niṣadhan in a voice choked with tears:

sanskrit: rājan paurajano dvāri tvāṃ didṛkṣur avasthitaḥ mantribhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvai rājabhaktipuraskṛtaḥ taṃ draṣṭum arhasīty evaṃ punaḥ punar abhāṣata
english: "O king, the townspeople stand at the door wishing to see you, accompanied by all the ministers, foremost in their devotion to the king. You should see them" — thus she spoke again and again.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā rucirāpāṅgīṃ vilapantīṃ sumadhyamām āviṣṭaḥ kalinā rājā nābhyabhāṣata kiṃ cana
english: But the king, possessed by Kali, said not a single word to her — that lovely-eyed, slender-waisted woman — as she lamented thus.

sanskrit: tatas te mantriṇaḥ sarve te caiva puravāsinaḥ nāyam astīti duḥkhārtā vrīḍitā jagmur ālayān
english: Then all those ministers and townspeople, afflicted with grief and ashamed, went home saying: "He is not himself anymore."

sanskrit: tathā tad abhavad dyūtaṃ puṣkarasya nalasya ca yudhiṣṭhira bahūn māsān puṇyaślokas tv ajīyata
english: And so that gambling match between Puṣkara and Nala went on for many months, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and the glorious Nala continued to lose.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca damayantī tato dṛṣṭvā puṇyaślokaṃ narādhipam unmattavad anunmattā devane gatacetasam
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then Damayantī, herself sane though witnessing the glorious king, that lord among men, behaving like a madman with his mind entirely consumed by gambling,

sanskrit: bhayaśokasamāviṣṭā rājan bhīmasutā tataḥ cintayām āsa tat kāryaṃ sumahat pārthivaṃ prati
english: overwhelmed by fear and grief, O king, the daughter of Bhīma then thought deeply about what great action needed to be taken concerning her husband.

sanskrit: sā śaṅkamānā tatpāpaṃ cikīrṣantī ca tatpriyam nalaṃ ca hṛtasarvasvam upalabhyedam abravīt
english: Suspecting the evil that was at work, yet wishing to do what was best for him, perceiving Nala stripped of all his wealth, she spoke as follows:

sanskrit: bṛhatsene vrajāmātyān ānāyya nalaśāsanāt ācakṣva yad dhṛtaṃ dravyam avaśiṣṭaṃ ca yad vasu
english: "Bṛhatsenā, go and bring the ministers here under Nala's authority, and find out what property has been taken and what wealth remains."

sanskrit: tatas te mantriṇaḥ sarve vijñāya nalaśāsanam api no bhāgadheyaṃ syād ity uktvā punar āvrajan
english: Then all the ministers, having understood the command of Nala, said: "Perhaps there may yet be some portion for us" — and again they came to him.

sanskrit: tās tu sarvāḥ prakṛtayo dvitīyaṃ samupasthitāḥ nyavedayad bhīmasutā na ca tat pratyanandata
english: When all the subjects had come a second time and Bhīma's daughter had reported it to him, he took no pleasure in it.

sanskrit: vākyam apratinandantaṃ bhartāram abhivīkṣya sā damayantī punar veśma vrīḍitā praviveśa ha
english: Seeing her husband taking no pleasure in what was said, Damayantī, ashamed, went back inside the house.

sanskrit: niśamya satataṃ cākṣān puṇyaślokaparāṅmukhān nalaṃ ca hṛtasarvasvaṃ dhātrīṃ punar uvāca ha
english: Having heard how the dice continually turned away from the glorious Nala, and seeing Nala stripped of everything, she again spoke to her nurse:

sanskrit: bṛhatsene punar gaccha vārṣṇeyaṃ nalaśāsanāt sūtam ānaya kalyāṇi mahat kāryam upasthitam
english: "Bṛhatsenā, go again; by Nala's authority bring the charioteer Vārṣṇeya here, O auspicious one — a great matter is at hand."

sanskrit: bṛhatsenā tu tac chrutvā damayantyāḥ prabhāṣitam vārṣṇeyam ānayām āsa puruṣair āptakāribhiḥ
english: Hearing Damayantī's words, Bṛhatsenā brought Vārṣṇeya there with the help of trusted men of action.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyaṃ tu tato bhaimī sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā girā uvāca deśakālajñā prāptakālam aninditā
english: Then Bhīma's daughter, knowing time and place, spoke fitting words to Vārṣṇeya with a soothing and gentle voice, that blameless one:

sanskrit: jānīṣe tvaṃ yathā rājā samyagvṛttaḥ sadā tvayi tasya tvaṃ viṣamasthasya sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "You know how the king has always treated you rightly; now that he is in distress, you should render him your help."

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi nṛpatiḥ puṣkareṇeha jīyate tathā tathāsya dyūte vai rāgo bhūyo 'bhivardhate
english: "The more the king loses to Puṣkara here, the more his craving for the dice increases."

sanskrit: yathā ca puṣkarasyākṣā vartante vaśavartinaḥ tathā viparyayaś cāpi nalasyākṣeṣu dṛśyate
english: "Just as Puṣkara's dice obey his will, so too is the reverse seen in Nala's dice."

sanskrit: suhṛtsvajanavākyāni yathāvan na śṛṇoti ca nūnaṃ manye na śeṣo 'sti naiṣadhasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "He does not properly heed the words of his friends and kinsmen; I believe that nothing of the great-souled Niṣadhan remains."

sanskrit: yatra me vacanaṃ rājā nābhinandati mohitaḥ śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapannāsmi sārathe kuru madvacaḥ na hi me śudhyate bhāvaḥ kadā cid vinaśed iti
english: "When the king, deluded, takes no pleasure even in my word, I take refuge in you, O charioteer — do as I say, for my heart cannot be set at rest with the thought that he might be destroyed."

sanskrit: nalasya dayitān aśvān yojayitvā mahājavān idam āropya mithunaṃ kuṇḍinaṃ yātum arhasi
english: "Harness Nala's beloved horses, those of great speed; place this pair of children upon the chariot and go to Kuṇḍina."

sanskrit: mama jñātiṣu nikṣipya dārakau syandanaṃ tathā aśvāṃś caitān yathākāmaṃ vasa vānyatra gaccha vā
english: "Having entrusted the two children and also the chariot and these horses to my kinsmen, you may remain there as you please, or go elsewhere."

sanskrit: damayantyās tu tad vākyaṃ vārṣṇeyo nalasārathiḥ nyavedayad aśeṣeṇa nalāmātyeṣu mukhyaśaḥ
english: Vārṣṇeya, Nala's charioteer, reported all of Damayantī's words in full to the chief ministers of Nala.

sanskrit: taiḥ sametya viniścitya so 'nujñāto mahīpate yayau mithunam āropya vidarbhāṃs tena vāhinā
english: Having met with them and decided, and having obtained permission from the ministers, O great king, he went to Vidarbha, having placed the pair upon that chariot.

sanskrit: hayāṃs tatra vinikṣipya sūto rathavaraṃ ca tam indrasenāṃ ca tāṃ kanyām indrasenaṃ ca bālakam
english: Having deposited the horses there, and that finest of chariots, and the girl Indrasenā, and the boy Indraseṇa,

sanskrit: āmantrya bhīmaṃ rājānam ārtaḥ śocan nalaṃ nṛpam aṭamānas tato 'yodhyāṃ jagāma nagarīṃ tadā
english: having taken leave of King Bhīma, distressed and grieving for King Nala, wandering about, the charioteer then went to the city of Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇaṃ sa rājānam upatasthe suduḥkhitaḥ bhṛtiṃ copayayau tasya sārathyena mahīpate
english: Deeply distressed, he presented himself to King Ṛtuparṇa, O great king, and entered his service as a charioteer.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tatas tu yāte vārṣṇeye puṇyaślokasya dīvyataḥ puṣkareṇa hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ yac cānyad vasu kiṃ cana
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, after Vārṣṇeya had departed while the glorious one was still gambling, Puṣkara won away his kingdom and whatever other wealth remained.

sanskrit: hṛtarājyaṃ nalaṃ rājan prahasan puṣkaro 'bravīt dyūtaṃ pravartatāṃ bhūyaḥ pratipāṇo 'sti kas tava
english: Laughing, Puṣkara said to Nala, whose kingdom had been taken: "Let the gambling continue; what stake do you still have to wager, O king?"

sanskrit: śiṣṭā te damayanty ekā sarvam anyad dhṛtaṃ mayā damayantyāḥ paṇaḥ sādhu vartatāṃ yadi manyase
english: "Only Damayantī remains to you; everything else has been won by me. Wager Damayantī — it would be good if you think so."

sanskrit: puṣkareṇaivam uktasya puṇyaślokasya manyunā vyadīryateva hṛdayaṃ na cainaṃ kiṃ cid abravīt
english: When Puṣkara had spoken thus to the glorious Nala, his heart seemed to split asunder with rage, yet he said not a word to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣkaram ālokya nalaḥ paramamanyumān utsṛjya sarvagātrebhyo bhūṣaṇāni mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then Nala, the greatly famous, looking at Puṣkara, his rage at its peak, stripped the ornaments from all his limbs.
